Classify Names as People, Organisations or Placeholders

Source: R/classify_names.R
classify_names.Rd

Officer lists hold more than people's names: banks and companies serving as trustees, notes such as SEE SCHEDULE O, and couples. classify_names() sorts each entry into one of five types, so that only people are matched as people.

Usage

classify_names(x, threshold = NULL)

Arguments

x

A character vector of raw names.

threshold

NULL (the default) for the thresholds above, or one number between 0 and 1 for all names.

Value

A data.frame with one row per input and columns name (the input), name_type and org_score (the model's probability that the name is an organisation, for a population with equal shares of people and organisations).

Details

  • "person": a person's name.

  • "organisation": an organisation (PNC BANK NA, TEAMSTERS LOCAL 338).

  • "person and organisation": a person's name followed by an organisation, usually an employer (JAMES LUISI NORTH END COMMUNITY HC). Parsing such a name usually still finds the person.

  • "several people": two or more people (MICHAEL AND ASHLEY SMITH).

  • "placeholder": a note instead of a name (SEE SCHEDULE O, VACANT, NO COMPENSATED OFFICERS), or nothing left after cleaning.

Placeholders and several people are found by rules. Organisations are found by a model: each word gets a score from how much more often it appears in organisation names than in people's names, and a logistic regression combines those scores with how many words the name has and how many are given names or surnames in census.names. The model was trained on Form 990 Part VII names, 2009-2025: 982,000 filer names and 9.4 million names from the person-name field (see data-raw/name_type_model.R and vignette("name-types")).

A name is an organisation when org_score reaches threshold. The default thresholds are stricter for names of one or two words (0.99) than for longer names (0.95), because short organisation names (MUNROE EAGLES) are hard to tell from people's names and most two-word entries are people.

Examples

classify_names(c("JOHN A SMITH", "PNC BANK NA", "SEE SCHEDULE O",
                 "MICHAEL AND ASHLEY SMITH", "TEAMSTERS LOCAL NO 338",
                 "JAMES LUISI NORTH END COMMUNITY HC"))
#>                                 name               name_type org_score
#> 1                       JOHN A SMITH                  person    0.0012
#> 2                        PNC BANK NA            organisation    0.9999
#> 3                     SEE SCHEDULE O             placeholder    0.0074
#> 4           MICHAEL AND ASHLEY SMITH          several people    0.0227
#> 5             TEAMSTERS LOCAL NO 338            organisation    0.9998
#> 6 JAMES LUISI NORTH END COMMUNITY HC person and organisation    0.9804
